cards.explanation: The answer is darkness and not light, friends, and Amos doesn't dress it up. He says, "It will be darkness and not light." (Amos 5:18) These people long for the Day of the LORD, and Amos asks them straight out what it will be for them. Wishing hard for a day doesn't change what the day is.

The answer is False. Amos says the man "…flees from a lion, only to encounter a bear…" (Amos 5:19) He gets away from one danger and runs right into another. Nobody in this picture gets to relax, friends, and I think that's the whole point of it.

The answer is a snake bite. Amos says the man "…enters his house and rests his hand against the wall, only to be bitten by a snake." (Amos 5:19) His own house! The one place a person figures is safe. I've leaned on plenty of walls in my day, friends, and I'm checking mine from now on.

The answer is that He hates and despises them. The LORD says it plainly: "I hate, I despise your feasts! I cannot stand the stench of your solemn assemblies." (Amos 5:21) Those are gatherings the people were holding, and the LORD says He cannot stand them. Then He keeps going, naming their offerings and their songs too. (Amos 5:22, 23)

The word is justice. The LORD says, "But let justice roll on like a river, and righteousness like an ever-flowing stream." (Amos 5:24) Justice is the river, and righteousness is the ever-flowing stream beside it. That's what He asks for, friends, right after turning down the songs and the offerings.

The word is idols, bakers. The LORD says, "You have taken along Sakkuth your king and Kaiwan your star god, the idols you made for yourselves." (Amos 5:26) Notice who made them: the people did. Their king and their star god, and the LORD calls both idols.

The answer is that He will send them into exile beyond Damascus. The LORD says, "Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Damascus…" (Amos 5:27) Damascus was a city, and beyond it means far from home. It's a heavy word, friends, and I think it's worth saying so. The one speaking is "…the God of Hosts."
